technical_issue: This item resolves the adviser's request to state where the system can run, how it is started and accessed, which technical components and operating roles it depends on, and which deployment, device, browser, connectivity, accessibility, capacity, and availability claims the study can support. It also prevents a local development setup from being described as a production service.
minimum_architecture_claim: The selected design is a client-server responsive web application. A React interface, styled with Tailwind CSS, runs in the user's web browser; a Laravel/PHP application performs authentication, server-side authorization, validation, workflow transitions, aggregation, SitRep generation, and audit recording; and MySQL persistently stores system records. Browser requests and server responses pass through HTTPS. The deployable service therefore needs, at minimum, a web server or reverse proxy, a supported PHP runtime with the extensions required by the selected Laravel release, the Laravel application and built React assets, a MySQL database, protected persistent storage for uploaded attachments and generated exports, application configuration and secrets, and DNS/TLS configuration for network access. A separate Node.js process is not necessarily a production runtime requirement when the React assets are compiled during build or deployment. Background queue workers, a scheduler, cache, mail or notification providers, object storage, and monitoring are required only if the implemented features actually use them. The exact Laravel, PHP, MySQL, Node, Tailwind, browser, operating-system, hosting-provider, and dependency versions are [uncertain] until they are fixed in lockfiles and a deployment specification; compatibility claims must follow those selected versions rather than the newest documentation by default.

runtime_and_deployment_requirements.client_access: Authorized users open an organization-issued HTTPS URL in a supported browser. Administrative and review work is intended for desktop or laptop browsers, while field reporting is intended to reflow for internet-capable smartphones and tablets. Users do not install a native application, and the browser is not the authority for permissions: each request is checked by the Laravel server for account, role, organization, jurisdiction, record state, and requested action.
runtime_and_deployment_requirements.server_location: The same architecture can run on a locally controlled institutional server or a contracted cloud/managed-hosting environment, provided the environment supplies the selected PHP/Laravel and MySQL versions, sufficient compute and storage, restricted administration, HTTPS, backups, monitoring, and a supportable network path. The thesis should name these as deployment options, not claim that all are implemented. A public production deployment should expose only the web entry point; Laravel's deployment guidance requires the web server to direct requests to public/index.php rather than serve the project root.
runtime_and_deployment_requirements.development_profile: Developers may run the application on individual computers or a private development network using XAMPP, Laravel Sail, Docker, or equivalent tools, with synthetic or de-identified test data. XAMPP's own documentation says it is intended for development rather than production. Localhost operation demonstrates startup and functions on that workstation; it does not demonstrate Internet availability, secure hosting, concurrent multi-organization use, or disaster resilience.
runtime_and_deployment_requirements.evaluation_profile: For alpha and beta evaluation, deploy a reproducible release to a controlled local-area server or test hosting environment, seed declared organizations and scenarios, and record the exact server build, device models or classes, operating systems, browser names and versions, screen sizes, connection conditions, dataset volume, and number of concurrent users tested. Any access outside a single isolated machine should use HTTPS and non-production credentials/data. Evaluation results apply only to those recorded conditions.
runtime_and_deployment_requirements.pilot_profile: A time-bounded pilot requires a named operator and customer owner, HTTPS, restricted production-like accounts, monitored application and database services, protected storage, tested backup restoration, incident/support contacts, maintenance notice, customer export, and agreed data-handling and retention rules. A pilot is not automatically a production-grade or 24-hour emergency service.
runtime_and_deployment_requirements.production_profile: Production use requires a hardened and supported server environment, patched dependencies, secret management, least-privilege service and database accounts, HTTPS with a valid certificate, monitoring and alerting, capacity testing, tested restore and continuity procedures, documented change/release/rollback processes, security and privacy review, service and support terms, and customer approval. The production topology, host, region/data location, redundancy model, availability target, recovery point objective, recovery time objective, capacity, browser matrix, and support hours are [uncertain] until selected, tested, and contractually assigned.
runtime_and_deployment_requirements.browser_and_device_baseline: Support must be declared from the actual compiled frontend and test matrix. React's browser DOM documentation describes use in popular browsers, but Tailwind CSS v4 depends on comparatively recent browser versions (Chrome 111, Safari 16.4, and Firefox 128 in its official compatibility page); therefore the paper must not promise every browser or infer support from React alone. If Tailwind v4 is selected, those versions provide an initial technical floor, subject to the exact utilities and build target used. Older browsers, embedded webviews, obsolete operating systems, rooted or compromised devices, unusual screen sizes, and assistive-technology combinations remain unsupported unless specifically tested. Responsive layout means adaptable presentation, not identical capability or performance on every device.
runtime_and_deployment_requirements.accessibility_baseline: Use WCAG 2.2 Level A and AA as the evaluation baseline for the implemented web content, including keyboard operation, visible focus, labels and instructions, error identification, reflow, orientation, pointer alternatives, touch target size, contrast, status messages, and non-color equivalents for charts. W3C states that WCAG applies across desktop and mobile devices but also states that conformance does not address every user need. Accessibility must therefore be reported as results from named automated checks and manual keyboard, screen-reader, zoom/reflow, and mobile interaction tests, not as a universal guarantee.

installation_and_operation.configuration_and_build: Pin and install the selected PHP/Composer and JavaScript dependencies from committed lockfiles; provide environment-specific configuration outside source control; set the application URL, database, mail/notification, storage, queue, session, cache, and logging settings actually used; generate a unique application key; compile the React/Tailwind production assets; and keep credentials and encryption keys out of the client bundle and repository. Production debug output must be disabled because Laravel warns that APP_DEBUG=true can expose sensitive configuration.
installation_and_operation.database_and_storage_setup: Create a least-privilege database account, run reviewed Laravel migrations against the intended database, create required initial platform/organization administrators through a controlled procedure, and configure protected persistent storage for attachments and generated files. Validate allowed file types, size limits, malware-handling procedure, available disk space, and backup inclusion before accepting real records. Schema changes need a tested deployment and rollback or forward-recovery plan; a migration command alone is not a recovery plan.
installation_and_operation.application_startup: The web server or reverse proxy terminates HTTPS and routes requests to Laravel's public/index.php. PHP processes the request, Laravel authenticates and authorizes it, applies validation/business rules, reads or writes MySQL and protected file storage, records relevant audit events, and returns data or a rendered response used by the browser interface. If asynchronous jobs are implemented, a queue worker must run under a process monitor; Laravel documents that queue workers are long-lived and must be restarted after deployment. If scheduled work is implemented, the deployment must also invoke the Laravel scheduler using the host's supported scheduling mechanism.
installation_and_operation.health_and_restart: Monitor HTTPS reachability plus dependencies that matter to the service, such as database access, writable storage, queue backlog/failures, certificate expiry, disk capacity, and backup status. Laravel provides a default /up route that reports whether the application booted, and its documentation permits application-specific checks, but a successful boot check alone does not prove that the database, storage, notification provider, or end-to-end reporting workflow works. Services should start automatically after host restart, and deployments should reload long-running services. Restart and failover behavior must be demonstrated rather than assumed.
installation_and_operation.maintenance: The platform operator applies operating-system and dependency security updates, renews certificates, monitors logs and resource use, rotates secrets where required, reviews failed jobs, performs backups, tests restoration, communicates maintenance, deploys tested releases, and maintains rollback or recovery instructions. Customer administrators maintain authorized users, role/jurisdiction assignments, workflow configuration, and prompt account deactivation. Maintenance windows may make the service temporarily unavailable and should be distinguished from unplanned outages.

dependencies_and_failure_conditions.electricity_and_connectivity: Clients need a powered compatible device and connectivity to the hosted service; the host and its network also need power and network availability. Slow, unstable, or interrupted connectivity can delay page loading, attachment upload, notification delivery, submission acknowledgement, and dashboard freshness. The interface should preserve an unfinished draft where practicable and clearly distinguish unsent, sending, received, failed, and retry states, but the current scope does not guarantee full offline operation or automatic conflict-free synchronization.
dependencies_and_failure_conditions.hosting_and_storage: Failure or maintenance of the web host, PHP service, MySQL server, DNS, TLS certificate, attachment storage, cache, queue, or notification provider can degrade or stop the dependent function. Local device storage is not the authoritative system record. A backup is useful only if it is complete, protected, retained, and restorable; MySQL's official guidance calls for regular backups, and its recovery guidance stresses practicing and verifying restore procedures in advance.
dependencies_and_failure_conditions.browser_and_device: Unsupported or outdated browsers may fail to render compiled CSS or execute application JavaScript; disabled cookies or JavaScript may prevent session or interface operation; a small display, low memory, damaged camera, denied permissions, or restricted file picker may limit reporting and attachments. The system does not repair client hardware, guarantee carrier coverage, or secure a device already controlled by an attacker.
dependencies_and_failure_conditions.external_services: Email, push, maps, geocoding, storage, or other external services are dependencies only if selected and implemented. Their outage, quota, rate limit, API change, inaccurate content, or delayed delivery must not silently change an official record or be treated as proof that an alert reached a user. The core record should preserve status and allow authorized users to see failed or pending dependent work. Live external-agency integration is outside scope unless an interface, authority, test environment, data contract, failure behavior, and completed test evidence are named.
dependencies_and_failure_conditions.personnel: Technical operation depends on a trained platform operator and support contact; official workflow depends on trained customer administrators, reporters, reviewers/verifiers, approvers, privacy/records personnel, and their timely action. Hosting cannot establish the truth of a field report, supply missing personnel, or ensure that users follow organizational procedures.

security_privacy_and_tenancy: All public network access should use HTTPS with a valid certificate and supported TLS configuration; NIST explains that TLS protects data during Internet transmission. Credentials, sessions, and personal or sensitive incident information must not be sent over plain HTTP. Laravel authorization must enforce organization, jurisdiction, role, object, and workflow-state rules on the server for reads, writes, searches, attachments, exports, dashboards, queued jobs, and audit data; hiding controls in React is not authorization. Use protected secrets, secure password hashing, least-privilege database/service accounts, secure session cookies, input validation, output encoding, upload controls, dependency updates, audit logging, and time-limited logged support access. The customer organization remains responsible for its lawful collection, users, disclosure, and official records, while the startup is responsible for the technical service and must follow documented processing authority. NPC Circular 2023-06 applies security duties to government and private-sector personal-data processing and requires business continuity that addresses backup, restoration, remedial time, periodic review, and testing. The prototype does not by itself prove compliance, certification, breach resistance, or tenant isolation; these require documented controls and negative cross-organization tests.
data_records_and_recovery: MySQL is the authoritative store for organization profiles, accounts, jurisdictions, report and verification versions, SitRep metadata, configuration versions, and audit events; protected file storage holds attachments and generated exports referenced by those records. Submitted or approved material should be versioned or superseded instead of silently overwritten. Record provenance should retain source organization/jurisdiction, author, observation/receipt/submission time with timezone, workflow state, decision actor/reason, source version, generated output version, and export event. The operator and customer records authority must define retention, legal holds, authorized export, archival transfer, and disposition; ordinary account deletion must not erase authorship. Backups must cover database and required files/configuration, be access-controlled and separated from the primary failure domain where appropriate, and be tested by restoration. Backup frequency, retention, encryption, storage location, RPO, RTO, maximum tolerable downtime, and offboarding deletion procedure are [uncertain] until risk assessment, customer authority, implementation, and restore measurements define them. A successful backup command is not proof of recoverability.

operator_and_owner.platform_operator: The startup or contracted hosting operator maintains servers and deployed software, configuration/secrets, TLS, monitoring, patches, releases, queue/scheduler processes where used, backups and restore tests, technical incidents, support, capacity evidence, and customer data export/offboarding. Any production-data access for support must be approved, purpose-limited, time-limited, least-privilege, and logged.
operator_and_owner.customer_organization: The DRRM organization appoints its organization administrator and authorized officials, supplies and validates jurisdiction/workflow configuration, manages user and role assignments, determines lawful collection/disclosure/retention, verifies field information, approves SitReps and official submissions, and maintains alternate operational channels for service outages.
operator_and_owner.shared_responsibility: Before pilot or production, the parties should document hosting location, service and maintenance windows, incident notification, support hours and severity handling, backup/restore objectives, subprocessors, security evidence, customer export, termination assistance, and authoritative contacts. The software team cannot silently assume either the startup or the LGU performs an unassigned duty.

human_decision_boundary: The software may accept structured input, apply syntactic/domain/range/consistency checks, flag possible duplicates or conflicts, route work, calculate traceable aggregates from stored records, assemble a draft SitRep from explicitly eligible versions, show source-linked dashboard summaries, and record decisions. It may not determine that an incident report is factually true, resolve conflicting evidence without an authorized reviewer, declare an emergency, select operational priorities, dispatch responders, allocate resources, approve or officially submit a SitRep, decide lawful disclosure or retention, or infer that no impact occurred because no digital report exists. Those actions remain with the customer's authorized officials or external authorities. System availability is an information-management aid, not a replacement for emergency communication and continuity procedures.
explicit_exclusions: No separate native mobile application, app-store distribution, guaranteed device integration, or background operation outside the browser.
No guaranteed full offline capture, synchronization, SMS/radio fallback, or uninterrupted reporting during loss of power, client connectivity, hosting, DNS, TLS, database, or storage.

No claim of support for every browser, device, operating system, webview, screen size, assistive technology, or low-bandwidth condition; support is limited to the declared test matrix and pinned frontend build.
No production use of XAMPP; its official FAQ limits it to development environments.

No guaranteed 24/7 availability, zero data loss, instant recovery, unlimited users/storage/attachments, fixed response time, geographic redundancy, or disaster-resilient hosting without measured architecture and agreed service objectives.
No predictive analytics, automated public warning, emergency dispatch, automatic resource allocation, independent factual verification, or automatic official submission.
No live national or third-party integration unless separately authorized, implemented, and tested; external-service delivery and accuracy are not guaranteed.

No claim that responsive design, HTTPS, cloud hosting, backups, WCAG-oriented implementation, or passing prototype tests alone establishes legal compliance, security certification, accessibility for every user, production readiness, procurement eligibility, nationwide suitability, commercial viability, or improved disaster outcomes.

evaluation_evidence.environment_inventory: Record source revision, dependency lockfiles, build identifier, server/hosting type, operating system, PHP/Laravel/MySQL versions, CPU/memory/storage, HTTPS/TLS result, database/storage/queue configuration, and whether each external provider is real, stubbed, or absent.
evaluation_evidence.client_matrix: Test the main role tasks on named current desktop and mobile browser versions and representative organization devices. Include viewport reflow/zoom, touch and keyboard operation, camera/file upload where implemented, session expiry, back/refresh behavior, download/export, and one unsupported-browser result. Do not publish a generic 'works on all devices' statement.
evaluation_evidence.network_and_failure_tests: Measure normal, throttled/high-latency, interrupted, and restored connections during draft saving, form submission, attachment upload, correction, verification, SitRep generation, and export. Confirm visible receipt/failure status, safe retry/idempotency, no duplicate committed reports, and recoverable drafts where promised. Exercise unavailable database/storage/queue/notification dependencies and verify safe failure without fabricated success.
evaluation_evidence.capacity_and_performance: Declare the seeded record count, attachment sizes, concurrent users or requests, test duration, hardware, endpoints/tasks, and percentile response times. Capacity claims must be bounded to these conditions; a small usability test is not a load test.
evaluation_evidence.security_and_isolation: Create at least two independently populated organizations and test direct object identifiers, list/search, attachments, exports, dashboard aggregates, queued/background actions, and audit logs across roles and tenants. Record prohibited requests blocked server-side. Also test authentication/session controls, upload rules, secret/debug exposure, dependency scanning, and HTTPS configuration. Passing tests reduces known risk but does not prove absence of vulnerabilities.
evaluation_evidence.recovery_and_operations: Restore a protected backup into a clean test environment, reconcile database records with attachments and generated outputs, measure achievable data-loss window and recovery time, verify service restart and health/dependency monitoring, and document failures. Use results to set, not merely assert, RPO/RTO and availability claims.
evaluation_evidence.accessibility: Evaluate applicable WCAG 2.2 A/AA criteria with automated tools plus manual keyboard, focus, error, reflow/zoom, screen-reader, touch-target, orientation, status-message, and chart alternative checks on the named client matrix. Report criteria tested, passes, failures, exceptions, assistive technologies, and tester conditions; do not infer universal accessibility from an automated score.
evaluation_evidence.acceptance_boundary: Prototype acceptance should require successful core reporting, review/correction, verification, SitRep generation, retrieval/export, dashboard drill-down, cross-organization isolation, interrupted-submission behavior, and backup restoration under declared conditions, with no unresolved critical data-integrity or access-control defect. Pilot/production approval additionally requires responsible owners, security/privacy assessment, operational procedures, service terms, and remediation of material findings.

recommended_thesis_wording:
Technically, the proposed system will be implemented as a connected, responsive client-server web application. The React and Tailwind CSS interface will execute in a supported browser on desktop, laptop, tablet, or smartphone devices, while a Laravel/PHP server will enforce authentication, organization- and role-scoped authorization, validation, reporting workflow, SitRep assembly, and audit recording. MySQL will store the operational records, and protected server storage will hold authorized attachments and generated files. Users will access the deployed service through an HTTPS address; no native mobile installation is included. The server may be deployed on a secured institutional server or contracted cloud environment that satisfies the selected Laravel/PHP and MySQL requirements. XAMPP or an equivalent local environment may be used for development and demonstration only, not as the claimed production host.

Operation requires configured application services, database migrations, compiled frontend assets, protected environment secrets, a valid TLS certificate, persistent storage, monitoring, backups, and restoration procedures. If asynchronous notifications or scheduled work are implemented, their queue workers and scheduler must also run as supervised services. The startup or contracted platform operator will maintain hosting, updates, certificates, monitoring, backups, restoration tests, and technical incidents; each customer organization will control its users, jurisdictions, workflow, verification, approval, disclosure, and official submission. Exact version, hosting, capacity, availability, browser-support, backup, and recovery claims will be limited to the configuration and conditions actually implemented and tested.

The application depends on compatible and adequately secured client devices, electricity, Internet connectivity, DNS, HTTPS, hosting, database and storage availability, and trained authorized personnel. Weak or interrupted connectivity may delay loading, upload, submission confirmation, notification, and dashboard updates. The interface may retain an unfinished draft and permit safe retry where implemented, but the project does not guarantee full offline synchronization, uninterrupted service, support for every browser or device, zero data loss, a fixed response time, or continuous 24-hour availability. Accessibility will be evaluated against applicable WCAG 2.2 Level A and AA criteria using named browsers, devices, and assistive technologies; the result will not be represented as accessibility for every user or configuration. The system organizes recorded information and generates traceable drafts and summaries, but authorized personnel remain responsible for factual verification, conflict resolution, SitRep approval, emergency decisions, and official communication.

authoritative_sources.title: Laravel 12.x Deployment
authoritative_sources.supported_proposition: Documents Laravel's server requirements, public/index.php web entry point, writable storage/cache directories, production optimization and debug warning, long-running service reload, and /up health route. The deployed project must use the documentation for its pinned Laravel release.

authoritative_sources.title: Laravel 12.x Queues
authoritative_sources.supported_proposition: Documents queue:work, the need for a process monitor in production, failed jobs and monitoring, and worker restart after deployment. These requirements apply only if the implementation uses queued work.

authoritative_sources.title: XAMPP FAQs for Windows
authoritative_sources.supported_proposition: The official XAMPP FAQ explicitly states that XAMPP is intended for development and is not production-ready.

authoritative_sources.title: React Client React DOM APIs
authoritative_sources.supported_proposition: Identifies React DOM client APIs as browser-side rendering APIs and discusses popular-browser support, but does not replace compatibility testing of the full compiled application.

authoritative_sources.title: Tailwind CSS Compatibility
authoritative_sources.supported_proposition: Tailwind CSS v4 is designed and tested for modern browsers and lists Chrome 111, Safari 16.4, and Firefox 128 as core dependency versions; the selected Tailwind major version materially affects the support matrix.

authoritative_sources.title: Tailwind CSS Responsive Design
authoritative_sources.supported_proposition: Documents viewport configuration and Tailwind's mobile-first breakpoint behavior; responsive utilities support adaptive presentation but do not establish device compatibility by themselves.

authoritative_sources.title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2
authoritative_sources.supported_proposition: W3C Recommendation defining testable, technology-neutral web accessibility criteria across desktop and mobile devices and noting that the guidelines do not address every user need.

authoritative_sources.title: W3C Mobile Accessibility
authoritative_sources.supported_proposition: Clarifies that WCAG covers web pages and applications used on mobile devices, including small screens, touch input, and different settings; there is no separate mobile-web accessibility standard.

authoritative_sources.title: NIST SP 800-52 Rev. 2: Guidelines for TLS Implementations
authoritative_sources.supported_proposition: Explains that TLS protects data transmitted over the Internet and provides protocol, certificate, cryptographic, and operational configuration guidance. It is a technical reference, not a claim of Philippine legal certification.

authoritative_sources.title: MySQL 8.4 Reference Manual: Establishing a Backup Policy
authoritative_sources.supported_proposition: States that useful backups must be scheduled regularly and describes full backup methods; the project must follow the documentation for its selected MySQL release and storage engine.

authoritative_sources.title: MySQL Enterprise Backup 8.4: Recovering or Restoring a Database Server
authoritative_sources.supported_proposition: Emphasizes confirming recovery duration, practicing and documenting restoration, and periodically verifying backup completeness before an incident. The operational principles apply even when another backup tool is selected.

authoritative_sources.title: NPC Circular No. 2023-06: Security of Personal Data in the Government and Private Sector
authoritative_sources.supported_proposition: Philippine privacy-security requirements for PICs and PIPs, including organizational, physical, and technical measures and business-continuity attention to backup, restoration, remedial time, disaster recovery, and periodic testing.

authoritative_sources.title: Implementing Rules and Regulations of the Data Privacy Act of 2012
authoritative_sources.supported_proposition: Requires appropriate organizational, physical, and technical safeguards, resilience and timely restoration, encryption and access controls where appropriate, and special controls for online access to government sensitive personal information.
